सजीवांमध्ये खूपसे वेगवेगळ्या प्रकारचे जीवरेणू उदा. कार्बोदके, प्रथिने (\(-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{N}}}-\) असतात), लिपिड (\(-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{O}-\) असतात) इ. असतात जे त्या संजीवांच्या संरचनेचा भाग असतात, आणि ते विविध शारीरिक अभिक्रियामध्ये भाग सुद्धा घेत असतात. म्हणजेच कार्बानी संयुगात, हायड्रोजन फक्त एक बंध, ऑक्सिजन फक्त दोन बंध, नायट्रोजन फक्त तीन बंध आणि कार्बन फक्त चार बंध तयार करतात.

Many organic compounds contain carbon (C), hydrogen (H), oxygen (O); and some of them also have additional elements such as nitrogen (N), halogens (X = Cl, Br, I) etc. The bond/s between the atoms in organic compounds are covalent, and are indicated by a ‘ - ’; eg. in methane, \(\mathrm{CH_4}\), each hydrogen and carbon has a single covalent bond.

Organic chemistry is also called the chemistry of functional groups (an atom or group of atoms that confers specific characteristics to that compound) eg. the functional group (FG) is hydroxyl, \(-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\) and the compounds formed are alcohols (R-O-H) where - R is alkyl group (\(-\mathrm{R}\) is \(-\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}}\) and ‘n’ is the number of carbon atoms). The FG carbonyl \(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\) has two arrangements: (i) aldehydic, \(-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) the compound is aldehyde (\(\mathrm{H}-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) or \(\mathrm{R}-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\)) and (ii) ketonic, \(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\) and the compound is ketone (\(\mathrm{R_1}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{R_2}\) where \(\mathrm{R_1}=\mathrm{R_2}\) or \(\mathrm{R_1}\neq\mathrm{R_2}\)). The combination of carbonyl group with hydroxyl group gives \(-\overset{\mathrm{OH}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) i.e. carboxyl functional group, and the compounds formed are carboxylic acids (\(\mathrm{H}-\overset{\mathrm{OH}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) and \(\mathrm{R}-\overset{\mathrm{OH}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\)). Carboxylic acids react with alcohols in presence of concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) yields esters, whose general formula is (\(\mathrm{H}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{OR}\) or \(\mathrm{R}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{OR_1}\) where \(\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{R_1}\) or \(\mathrm{R}\neq\mathrm{R_1}\)). The characteristic properties of esters are because of \(-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{O}-\) functional group.

Bodies of living organisms contain large number of different biomolecules eg. carbohydrates, proteins (contain \(-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{N}}}-\)), lipids (contain \(-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{O}-\)) etc. which constitute their structure, and are also part of various physiological processes taking place in them. Thus, hydrogen forms only one, oxygen forms only two, nitrogen forms only three, and carbon forms only four covalent bonds.

Though most of carbohydrates are represented by a general formula \(\mathrm{C_x(H_2O)_y}\) i.e. hydrates of carbon, they are chemically polyhydroxy aldehydes (or ketones) eg. \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\) is either glucose or fructose or galactose. They cannot be hydrolyzed further, hence are called monosaccharides. Disaccharides eg. sucrose, \(\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}\), on hydrolysis (using one \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)) yields two molecules of monosaccharides: glucose and fructose. Trisaccharides eg. raffinose, \(\mathrm{C_{18}H_{32}O_{16}}\), on hydrolysis (using two \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)) yields three monosaccharides one unit of each: glucose, fructose and galactose. Polysaccharide eg. starch, \(\mathrm{(C_6H_{10}O_5)_n}\), is a common ingredient of food grain, on hydrolysis yields a very large number of units of glucose.

Monosaccharide with an aldehydic carbonyl group is called aldose, and their names will have suffix ‘ose’ eg. Mannose, \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\). While that with a ketonic carbonyl group is called ketose, and their some names end with ‘ulose’. These names are further modified in accordance with the total number of carbon atoms in the monosaccharide eg. Mannose, \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\) can also be called aldohexose.

The smallest aldose, and the only one whose name does not end in “ose”, is glyceraldehyde. It has a chiral center or has an asymmetric carbon* atom (a carbon atom bonded to four different atoms or groups). A molecule with a chiral center has a pair of enantiomers which are related to each other as object and its mirror image. Each isomer of this pair rotates the plane polarized light in equal magnitude but in opposite directions.

\(\begin{array}{rcl} & \mathrm{H}\;\diagdown\;\diagup\!\!\diagup\;\mathrm{O} & \\ & \mathrm{C} & \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C^{*}} & -\mathrm{H} \\ & | & \\ & \mathrm{CH_2OH} & \end{array}\)
Glyceraldehyde

This property (optical activity) is shown only by those organic compounds which have a chiral center. One can arrive at the number of optical isomers using the relation \(2^n\), where n is the number of chiral centers. The molecules having the same molecular formula but different structures are called isomers. If the isomers carry different functional groups, they are called functional isomers, and the phenomenon is called functional isomerism.

जरी कार्बोदकांचे सर्वसामान्य सूत्र \(\mathrm{C_x(H_2O)_y}\), म्हणजेच कार्बनचे सजल असले तरी रासायनिक दृष्ट्या ते पॉलीहायड्रोक्सी अल्डिहाइड (किंवा कीटोन) असतात उदा. \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\), हे एकतर ग्लुकोज किंवा फ्रूक्टोज किंवा गॅल्याक्टोज असते. ह्यांचे जलीय अपघटण करता येत नाही म्हणूनच त्यांना मोनोसॅकॅराईड म्हणतात. डायसॅकॅराईड उदा. \(\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}\), सुक्रोजचे जलीय अपघटण (एक \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) वापरून) होऊन दोन मोनोसॅकॅराईड म्हणजेच ग्लुकोज आणि फ्रूक्टोज मिळतात. ट्रायसॅकॅराइड उदा. \(\mathrm{C_{18}H_{32}O_{16}}\), रॅफीनोजचे जलीय अपघटण (दोन \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) वापरून) होऊन तीन मोनोसॅकॅराईड म्हणजेच ग्लुकोज, गॅल्याक्टोज, आणि फ्रूक्टोजचे प्रत्येकी एक एकक मिळतात. पॉलिसॅकॅराईड उदा. \(\mathrm{(C_6H_{10}O_5)_n}\), स्टार्चचे जलीय अपघटण होऊन ग्लुकोजची खूपच एकक तयार होतात.

en.context:
Many organic compounds contain carbon (C), hydrogen (H), oxygen (O); and some of them also have additional elements such as nitrogen (N), halogens (X = Cl, Br, I) etc. The bond/s between the atoms in organic compounds are covalent, and are indicated by a ‘ - ’; eg. in methane, \(\mathrm{CH_4}\), each hydrogen and carbon has a single covalent bond.

Organic chemistry is also called the chemistry of functional groups (an atom or group of atoms that confers specific characteristics to that compound) eg. the functional group (FG) is hydroxyl, \(-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\) and the compounds formed are alcohols (R-O-H) where - R is alkyl group (\(-\mathrm{R}\) is \(-\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}}\) and ‘n’ is the number of carbon atoms). The FG carbonyl \(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\) has two arrangements: (i) aldehydic, \(-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) the compound is aldehyde (\(\mathrm{H}-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) or \(\mathrm{R}-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\)) and (ii) ketonic, \(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\) and the compound is ketone (\(\mathrm{R_1}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{R_2}\) where \(\mathrm{R_1}=\mathrm{R_2}\) or \(\mathrm{R_1}\neq\mathrm{R_2}\)). The combination of carbonyl group with hydroxyl group gives \(-\overset{\mathrm{OH}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) i.e. carboxyl functional group, and the compounds formed are carboxylic acids (\(\mathrm{H}-\overset{\mathrm{OH}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) and \(\mathrm{R}-\overset{\mathrm{OH}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\)). Carboxylic acids react with alcohols in presence of concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) yields esters, whose general formula is (\(\mathrm{H}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{OR}\) or \(\mathrm{R}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{OR_1}\) where \(\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{R_1}\) or \(\mathrm{R}\neq\mathrm{R_1}\)). The characteristic properties of esters are because of \(-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{O}-\) functional group.

Bodies of living organisms contain large number of different biomolecules eg. carbohydrates, proteins (contain \(-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{N}}}-\)), lipids (contain \(-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{O}-\)) etc. which constitute their structure, and are also part of various physiological processes taking place in them. Thus, hydrogen forms only one, oxygen forms only two, nitrogen forms only three, and carbon forms only four covalent bonds.

Though most of carbohydrates are represented by a general formula \(\mathrm{C_x(H_2O)_y}\) i.e. hydrates of carbon, they are chemically polyhydroxy aldehydes (or ketones) eg. \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\) is either glucose or fructose or galactose. They cannot be hydrolyzed further, hence are called monosaccharides. Disaccharides eg. sucrose, \(\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}\), on hydrolysis (using one \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)) yields two molecules of monosaccharides: glucose and fructose. Trisaccharides eg. raffinose, \(\mathrm{C_{18}H_{32}O_{16}}\), on hydrolysis (using two \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)) yields three monosaccharides one unit of each: glucose, fructose and galactose. Polysaccharide eg. starch, \(\mathrm{(C_6H_{10}O_5)_n}\), is a common ingredient of food grain, on hydrolysis yields a very large number of units of glucose.

Monosaccharide with an aldehydic carbonyl group is called aldose, and their names will have suffix ‘ose’ eg. Mannose, \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\). While that with a ketonic carbonyl group is called ketose, and their some names end with ‘ulose’. These names are further modified in accordance with the total number of carbon atoms in the monosaccharide eg. Mannose, \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\) can also be called aldohexose.

The smallest aldose, and the only one whose name does not end in “ose”, is glyceraldehyde. It has a chiral center or has an asymmetric carbon* atom (a carbon atom bonded to four different atoms or groups). A molecule with a chiral center has a pair of enantiomers which are related to each other as object and its mirror image. Each isomer of this pair rotates the plane polarized light in equal magnitude but in opposite directions.

\(\begin{array}{rcl} & \mathrm{H}\;\diagdown\;\diagup\!\!\diagup\;\mathrm{O} & \\ & \mathrm{C} & \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C^{*}} & -\mathrm{H} \\ & | & \\ & \mathrm{CH_2OH} & \end{array}\)
Glyceraldehyde

This property (optical activity) is shown only by those organic compounds which have a chiral center. One can arrive at the number of optical isomers using the relation \(2^n\), where n is the number of chiral centers. The molecules having the same molecular formula but different structures are called isomers. If the isomers carry different functional groups, they are called functional isomers, and the phenomenon is called functional isomerism.

Many organic compounds contain carbon (C), hydrogen (H), oxygen (O); and some of them also have additional elements such as nitrogen (N), halogens (X = Cl, Br, I) etc. The bond/s between the atoms in organic compounds are covalent, and are indicated by a ‘ - ’; eg. in methane, \(\mathrm{CH_4}\), each hydrogen and carbon has a single covalent bond.

Organic chemistry is also called the chemistry of functional groups (an atom or group of atoms that confers specific characteristics to that compound) eg. the functional group (FG) is hydroxyl, \(-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\) and the compounds formed are alcohols (R-O-H) where - R is alkyl group (\(-\mathrm{R}\) is \(-\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}}\) and ‘n’ is the number of carbon atoms). The FG carbonyl \(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\) has two arrangements: (i) aldehydic, \(-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) the compound is aldehyde (\(\mathrm{H}-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) or \(\mathrm{R}-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\)) and (ii) ketonic, \(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\) and the compound is ketone (\(\mathrm{R_1}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{R_2}\) where \(\mathrm{R_1}=\mathrm{R_2}\) or \(\mathrm{R_1}\neq\mathrm{R_2}\)). The combination of carbonyl group with hydroxyl group gives \(-\overset{\mathrm{OH}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) i.e. carboxyl functional group, and the compounds formed are carboxylic acids (\(\mathrm{H}-\overset{\mathrm{OH}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) and \(\mathrm{R}-\overset{\mathrm{OH}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\)). Carboxylic acids react with alcohols in presence of concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) yields esters, whose general formula is (\(\mathrm{H}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{OR}\) or \(\mathrm{R}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{OR_1}\) where \(\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{R_1}\) or \(\mathrm{R}\neq\mathrm{R_1}\)). The characteristic properties of esters are because of \(-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{O}-\) functional group.

Bodies of living organisms contain large number of different biomolecules eg. carbohydrates, proteins (contain \(-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{N}}}-\)), lipids (contain \(-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{O}-\)) etc. which constitute their structure, and are also part of various physiological processes taking place in them. Thus, hydrogen forms only one, oxygen forms only two, nitrogen forms only three, and carbon forms only four covalent bonds.

Though most of carbohydrates are represented by a general formula \(\mathrm{C_x(H_2O)_y}\) i.e. hydrates of carbon, they are chemically polyhydroxy aldehydes (or ketones) eg. \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\) is either glucose or fructose or galactose. They cannot be hydrolyzed further, hence are called monosaccharides. Disaccharides eg. sucrose, \(\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}\), on hydrolysis (using one \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)) yields two molecules of monosaccharides: glucose and fructose. Trisaccharides eg. raffinose, \(\mathrm{C_{18}H_{32}O_{16}}\), on hydrolysis (using two \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)) yields three monosaccharides one unit of each: glucose, fructose and galactose. Polysaccharide eg. starch, \(\mathrm{(C_6H_{10}O_5)_n}\), is a common ingredient of food grain, on hydrolysis yields a very large number of units of glucose.

Monosaccharide with an aldehydic carbonyl group is called aldose, and their names will have suffix ‘ose’ eg. Mannose, \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\). While that with a ketonic carbonyl group is called ketose, and their some names end with ‘ulose’. These names are further modified in accordance with the total number of carbon atoms in the monosaccharide eg. Mannose, \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\) can also be called aldohexose.

The smallest aldose, and the only one whose name does not end in “ose”, is glyceraldehyde. It has a chiral center or has an asymmetric carbon* atom (a carbon atom bonded to four different atoms or groups). A molecule with a chiral center has a pair of enantiomers which are related to each other as object and its mirror image. Each isomer of this pair rotates the plane polarized light in equal magnitude but in opposite directions.

This property (optical activity) is shown only by those organic compounds which have a chiral center. One can arrive at the number of optical isomers using the relation \(2^n\), where n is the number of chiral centers. The molecules having the same molecular formula but different structures are called isomers. If the isomers carry different functional groups, they are called functional isomers, and the phenomenon is called functional isomerism.

\(\begin{array}{rcl} & \mathrm{CHO} & \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{H} \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{H} \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{H}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{OH} \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{H}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{OH} \\ & | & \\ & \mathrm{CH_2OH} & \end{array}\)

OR

\(\begin{array}{rcl} & \mathrm{H}\;\diagdown\;\diagup\!\!\diagup\;\mathrm{O} & \\ & \mathrm{C} & \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C^{*}} & -\mathrm{H} \\ & | & \\ & \mathrm{CH_2OH} & \end{array}\)

हा गुणधर्म फक्त ज्याच्या कार्बनी संयुगाच्या रेणूमध्ये कायरल केंद्र असेल अशीच कार्बनी संयुगे दर्शवितात. आपण त्या रेणूमधील अशा प्रतिबिंबिरूपितांची संख्या \(2^n\) (जेव्हा n = कायरल केंद्रांची त्या रेणूमधील संख्या). ज्यांचे रेणुसूत्र सारखे असून रेणूंच्या भिन्न संरचनांना समसूत्री म्हणतात. जर समसूत्रीमध्ये विविध क्रियात्मक गट असणाऱ्यांना क्रियात्मक गट समसूत्री, आणि ह्या घटनेला क्रियात्मक गट समसूत्रता म्हणतात.

en.stem: The compound \(\begin{array}{rcl} & \mathrm{CH_2OH} & \\ & | & \\ & \mathrm{C} & =\mathrm{O} \\ & | & \\ (\mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{H})_3 \\ & | & \\ & \mathrm{CH_2OH} & \end{array}\) is a ______ and has ______ pairs of optical isomers.
en.context:
Many organic compounds contain carbon (C), hydrogen (H), oxygen (O); and some of them also have additional elements such as nitrogen (N), halogens (X = Cl, Br, I) etc. The bond/s between the atoms in organic compounds are covalent, and are indicated by a ‘ - ’; eg. in methane, \(\mathrm{CH_4}\), each hydrogen and carbon has a single covalent bond.

Organic chemistry is also called the chemistry of functional groups (an atom or group of atoms that confers specific characteristics to that compound) eg. the functional group (FG) is hydroxyl, \(-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\) and the compounds formed are alcohols (R-O-H) where - R is alkyl group (\(-\mathrm{R}\) is \(-\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}}\) and ‘n’ is the number of carbon atoms). The FG carbonyl \(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\) has two arrangements: (i) aldehydic, \(-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) the compound is aldehyde (\(\mathrm{H}-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) or \(\mathrm{R}-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\)) and (ii) ketonic, \(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\) and the compound is ketone (\(\mathrm{R_1}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{R_2}\) where \(\mathrm{R_1}=\mathrm{R_2}\) or \(\mathrm{R_1}\neq\mathrm{R_2}\)). The combination of carbonyl group with hydroxyl group gives \(-\overset{\mathrm{OH}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) i.e. carboxyl functional group, and the compounds formed are carboxylic acids (\(\mathrm{H}-\overset{\mathrm{OH}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) and \(\mathrm{R}-\overset{\mathrm{OH}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\)). Carboxylic acids react with alcohols in presence of concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) yields esters, whose general formula is (\(\mathrm{H}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{OR}\) or \(\mathrm{R}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{OR_1}\) where \(\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{R_1}\) or \(\mathrm{R}\neq\mathrm{R_1}\)). The characteristic properties of esters are because of \(-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{O}-\) functional group.

Bodies of living organisms contain large number of different biomolecules eg. carbohydrates, proteins (contain \(-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{N}}}-\)), lipids (contain \(-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{O}-\)) etc. which constitute their structure, and are also part of various physiological processes taking place in them. Thus, hydrogen forms only one, oxygen forms only two, nitrogen forms only three, and carbon forms only four covalent bonds.

Though most of carbohydrates are represented by a general formula \(\mathrm{C_x(H_2O)_y}\) i.e. hydrates of carbon, they are chemically polyhydroxy aldehydes (or ketones) eg. \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\) is either glucose or fructose or galactose. They cannot be hydrolyzed further, hence are called monosaccharides. Disaccharides eg. sucrose, \(\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}\), on hydrolysis (using one \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)) yields two molecules of monosaccharides: glucose and fructose. Trisaccharides eg. raffinose, \(\mathrm{C_{18}H_{32}O_{16}}\), on hydrolysis (using two \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)) yields three monosaccharides one unit of each: glucose, fructose and galactose. Polysaccharide eg. starch, \(\mathrm{(C_6H_{10}O_5)_n}\), is a common ingredient of food grain, on hydrolysis yields a very large number of units of glucose.

Monosaccharide with an aldehydic carbonyl group is called aldose, and their names will have suffix ‘ose’ eg. Mannose, \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\). While that with a ketonic carbonyl group is called ketose, and their some names end with ‘ulose’. These names are further modified in accordance with the total number of carbon atoms in the monosaccharide eg. Mannose, \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\) can also be called aldohexose.

\(\begin{array}{rcl} & \mathrm{CHO} & \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{H} \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{H} \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{H}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{OH} \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{H}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{OH} \\ & | & \\ & \mathrm{CH_2OH} & \end{array}\)
Structure of mannose

OR

\(\begin{array}{rcl} & \mathrm{CHO} & \\ & | & \\ (\mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{H})_4 \\ & | & \\ & \mathrm{CH_2OH} & \end{array}\)
Structure of mannose

The smallest aldose, and the only one whose name does not end in “ose”, is glyceraldehyde. It has a chiral center or has an asymmetric carbon* atom (a carbon atom bonded to four different atoms or groups). A molecule with a chiral center has a pair of enantiomers which are related to each other as object and its mirror image. Each isomer of this pair rotates the plane polarized light in equal magnitude but in opposite directions.

\(\begin{array}{rcl} & \mathrm{H}\;\diagdown\;\diagup\!\!\diagup\;\mathrm{O} & \\ & \mathrm{C} & \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C^{*}} & -\mathrm{H} \\ & | & \\ & \mathrm{CH_2OH} & \end{array}\)
Glyceraldehyde

This property (optical activity) is shown only by those organic compounds which have a chiral center. One can arrive at the number of optical isomers using the relation \(2^n\), where n is the number of chiral centers. The molecules having the same molecular formula but different structures are called isomers. If the isomers carry different functional groups, they are called functional isomers, and the phenomenon is called functional isomerism.

जरी कार्बोदकांचे सर्वसामान्य सूत्र \(\mathrm{C_x(H_2O)_y}\), म्हणजेच कार्बनचे सजल असले तरी रासायनिक दृष्ट्या ते पॉलीहायड्रोक्सी अल्डिहाइड (किंवा कीटोन) असतात उदा. \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\), हे एकतर ग्लुकोज किंवा फ्रूक्टोज किंवा गॅल्याक्टोज असते. ह्यांचे जलीय अपघटण करता येत नाही म्हणूनच त्यांना मोनोसॅकॅराईड म्हणतात. डायसॅकॅराईड उदा. \(\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}\), सुक्रोजचे जलीय अपघटण (एक \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) वापरून) होऊन दोन मोनोसॅकॅराईड म्हणजेच ग्लुकोज आणि फ्रूक्टोज मिळतात. ट्रायसॅकॅराइड उदा. \(\mathrm{C_{18}H_{32}O_{16}}\), रॅफीनोजचे जलीय अपघटण (दोन \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) वापरून) होऊन तीन मोनोसॅकॅराईड म्हणजेच ग्लुकोज, गॅल्याक्टोज, आणि फ्रूक्टोजचे प्रत्येकी एक एकक मिळतात. पॉलिसॅकॅराईड उदा. \(\mathrm{(C_6H_{10}O_5)_n}\), स्टार्चचे जलीय अपघटण होऊन ग्लुकोजची खूपच एकक तयार होतात.

ज्या मोनोसॅकॅराईडमध्ये एक अल्डिहाइडीक क्रियात्मक गट असतो त्याला अल्डोज म्हणतात, आणि त्यांच्या नावांचा शेवट ‘ओज’ ने करतात उदा. मॅनोज \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\), तसेच ज्यामध्ये एक किटॉनिक क्रियात्मक गट असतो त्याला किटोज म्हणतात, आणि त्यातल्या काहींच्या नावांचा शेवट ‘युलोज’ ने करतात. ह्या नावांचे त्या मोनोसॅकॅराईडच्या रेणूमध्ये असलेल्या कार्बन अणुंच्या संखेनुसार आणखी परिवर्तन होते उदा. मॅनोज \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\) चे नाव अल्डोहेक्झोज असे सुद्धा ठरते.

\(\begin{array}{rcl} & \mathrm{CHO} & \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{H} \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{H} \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{H}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{OH} \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{H}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{OH} \\ & | & \\ & \mathrm{CH_2OH} & \end{array}\)
मॅनोजची संरचना

OR

\(\begin{array}{rcl} & \mathrm{CHO} & \\ & | & \\ (\mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{H})_4 \\ & | & \\ & \mathrm{CH_2OH} & \end{array}\)
मॅनोजची संरचना

सगळ्यात लहान अल्डोज, आणि फक्त ज्याच्या नावाचा शेवट ‘‘ओज’’ होत नाही तो ग्लिसेरालडिहाइड आहे. त्यात एक कायरल केंद्र किंवा एक असममितिय कार्बन* अणु (जो कार्बनचा अणु वेगवेगळ्या मूलद्रव्यांच्या अणुंना किंवा अणुंच्या विविध गटांना जोडलेला असतो) आहे. एक कायरल केंद्र असणारे रेणू प्रतिबिंबिरूपितांच्या एक जोडीच्या रूपात अस्तित्वात असतात आणि त्यांचे एकमेकाशी संबंध हे वस्तु आणि त्याची दर्पण प्रतिमा असे असते. ह्या जोडीतील प्रत्येक प्रतिबिंबिरूपित, प्रतल ध्रुविय प्रकाश सारख्याच मात्रेत पण विरुद्ध दिशांना वळवतात/ परिवलन करतात.

\(\begin{array}{rcl} & \mathrm{H}\;\diagdown\;\diagup\!\!\diagup\;\mathrm{O} & \\ & \mathrm{C} & \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C^{*}} & -\mathrm{H} \\ & | & \\ & \mathrm{CH_2OH} & \end{array}\)
ग्लिसेरालडीहाइड

हा गुणधर्म फक्त ज्याच्या कार्बनी संयुगाच्या रेणूमध्ये कायरल केंद्र असेल अशीच कार्बनी संयुगे दर्शवितात. आपण त्या रेणूमधील अशा प्रतिबिंबिरूपितांची संख्या \(2^n\) (जेव्हा n = कायरल केंद्रांची त्या रेणूमधील संख्या). ज्यांचे रेणुसूत्र सारखे असून रेणूंच्या भिन्न संरचनांना समसूत्री म्हणतात. जर समसूत्रीमध्ये विविध क्रियात्मक गट असणाऱ्यांना क्रियात्मक गट समसूत्री, आणि ह्या घटनेला क्रियात्मक गट समसूत्रता म्हणतात.

en.stem: Which of the following compounds will show optical activity ?
en.context:
Many organic compounds contain carbon (C), hydrogen (H), oxygen (O); and some of them also have additional elements such as nitrogen (N), halogens (X = Cl, Br, I) etc. The bond/s between the atoms in organic compounds are covalent, and are indicated by a ‘ - ’; eg. in methane, \(\mathrm{CH_4}\), each hydrogen and carbon has a single covalent bond.

Organic chemistry is also called the chemistry of functional groups (an atom or group of atoms that confers specific characteristics to that compound) eg. the functional group (FG) is hydroxyl, \(-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\) and the compounds formed are alcohols (R-O-H) where - R is alkyl group (\(-\mathrm{R}\) is \(-\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}}\) and ‘n’ is the number of carbon atoms). The FG carbonyl \(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\) has two arrangements: (i) aldehydic, \(-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) the compound is aldehyde (\(\mathrm{H}-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) or \(\mathrm{R}-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\)) and (ii) ketonic, \(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\) and the compound is ketone (\(\mathrm{R_1}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{R_2}\) where \(\mathrm{R_1}=\mathrm{R_2}\) or \(\mathrm{R_1}\neq\mathrm{R_2}\)). The combination of carbonyl group with hydroxyl group gives \(-\overset{\mathrm{OH}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) i.e. carboxyl functional group, and the compounds formed are carboxylic acids (\(\mathrm{H}-\overset{\mathrm{OH}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\) and \(\mathrm{R}-\overset{\mathrm{OH}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{C}}}=\mathrm{O}\)). Carboxylic acids react with alcohols in presence of concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) yields esters, whose general formula is (\(\mathrm{H}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{OR}\) or \(\mathrm{R}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{OR_1}\) where \(\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{R_1}\) or \(\mathrm{R}\neq\mathrm{R_1}\)). The characteristic properties of esters are because of \(-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{O}-\) functional group.

Bodies of living organisms contain large number of different biomolecules eg. carbohydrates, proteins (contain \(-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\overset{\mathrm{H}}{\overset{|}{\mathrm{N}}}-\)), lipids (contain \(-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\overset{\|}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{O}-\)) etc. which constitute their structure, and are also part of various physiological processes taking place in them. Thus, hydrogen forms only one, oxygen forms only two, nitrogen forms only three, and carbon forms only four covalent bonds.

Though most of carbohydrates are represented by a general formula \(\mathrm{C_x(H_2O)_y}\) i.e. hydrates of carbon, they are chemically polyhydroxy aldehydes (or ketones) eg. \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\) is either glucose or fructose or galactose. They cannot be hydrolyzed further, hence are called monosaccharides. Disaccharides eg. sucrose, \(\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}\), on hydrolysis (using one \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)) yields two molecules of monosaccharides: glucose and fructose. Trisaccharides eg. raffinose, \(\mathrm{C_{18}H_{32}O_{16}}\), on hydrolysis (using two \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)) yields three monosaccharides one unit of each: glucose, fructose and galactose. Polysaccharide eg. starch, \(\mathrm{(C_6H_{10}O_5)_n}\), is a common ingredient of food grain, on hydrolysis yields a very large number of units of glucose.

Monosaccharide with an aldehydic carbonyl group is called aldose, and their names will have suffix ‘ose’ eg. Mannose, \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\). While that with a ketonic carbonyl group is called ketose, and their some names end with ‘ulose’. These names are further modified in accordance with the total number of carbon atoms in the monosaccharide eg. Mannose, \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\) can also be called aldohexose.

\(\begin{array}{rcl} & \mathrm{CHO} & \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{H} \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{H} \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{H}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{OH} \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{H}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{OH} \\ & | & \\ & \mathrm{CH_2OH} & \end{array}\)
Structure of mannose

OR

\(\begin{array}{rcl} & \mathrm{CHO} & \\ & | & \\ (\mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C} & -\mathrm{H})_4 \\ & | & \\ & \mathrm{CH_2OH} & \end{array}\)
Structure of mannose

The smallest aldose, and the only one whose name does not end in “ose”, is glyceraldehyde. It has a chiral center or has an asymmetric carbon* atom (a carbon atom bonded to four different atoms or groups). A molecule with a chiral center has a pair of enantiomers which are related to each other as object and its mirror image. Each isomer of this pair rotates the plane polarized light in equal magnitude but in opposite directions.

\(\begin{array}{rcl} & \mathrm{H}\;\diagdown\;\diagup\!\!\diagup\;\mathrm{O} & \\ & \mathrm{C} & \\ & | & \\ \mathrm{HO}- & \mathrm{C^{*}} & -\mathrm{H} \\ & | & \\ & \mathrm{CH_2OH} & \end{array}\)
Glyceraldehyde

This property (optical activity) is shown only by those organic compounds which have a chiral center. One can arrive at the number of optical isomers using the relation \(2^n\), where n is the number of chiral centers. The molecules having the same molecular formula but different structures are called isomers. If the isomers carry different functional groups, they are called functional isomers, and the phenomenon is called functional isomerism.
